inputs.sequence_prompt:
Continue this exact live-action moment in one uninterrupted fifteen-second shot. Preserve the three real actors, faces, hair, proportions, costumes and carried objects from the supplied frame. Same wooden airship deck, rigid red curved staircase at center-right, brass railings, cabin door and porthole below, gold fixture on upper deck at right, fixed stone theatre at left, blue-hour sky and steady warm lantern light. No change of location or internal cut. The ship is still docked; the exterior gangway and closed gate remain stationary throughout.
Start precisely from the supplied positions: Celes, blonde hair tied high with blue ribbon, ivory gown and blue sash, is ALREADY partway up the existing stairs with her hand reaching the upper rail. Locke, brown-haired with blue bandana, dark jacket, blue trousers and cream boots, is at the foot of the stairs behind her, holding his single wooden shield in his LEFT hand, sword sheathed. Setzer, silver-haired and wearing the long black coat with pale lapels, is ALREADY standing on the upper deck behind the brass railing, watching them. There are only these three people.
During seconds zero to five, Celes continues the upward step already underway. She keeps her free hand on the existing rail and holds her gown hem clear of her shoes with the other hand. Her shoes find the remaining wooden treads one after another; knees bend, weight transfers onto each solid tread. She steps through the existing stair opening onto the upper landing, never through the brass railing. Setzer takes two short sideways steps to his right on the upper deck to clear her landing space. He stays upright, watches her arrival and then looks down toward Locke. Locke waits for two clear treads between himself and Celes, then places his right hand on the existing rail and begins ascending, keeping his shield close to his left thigh.
During seconds five to eleven, Celes takes two steps away from the top stair onto the upper deck, releases the gathered hem so her gown falls naturally, then turns her head back toward Locke. Locke steadily climbs the same existing staircase. His cream boots land on successive wooden treads; his right hand slides along the solid side rail; his shield stays in his left hand clear of his knees. He rises by walking UP the treads, never jumping or floating. His whole path from the lower stair to the upper landing remains spatially connected and visible. Setzer waits beside the upper landing, out of his path. The steps, curved stair sides, brass posts and cabin remain rigid and unchanged. No actor intersects another actor, the railing, or the wooden floor.
During the final four seconds, Locke places his final boot onto the upper deck and straightens, looking toward Setzer. Only after Locke reaches the landing, Setzer looks at both companions and says clearly in a calm mature male voice, natural Brazilian Portuguese, with matching lips: <d>[Portuguese] Por aqui. Vamos preparar a partida.</d> He indicates the clear route along the upper deck with one brief open-handed gesture, turns and takes two purposeful steps to screen right. Celes turns toward him and begins to follow. Locke, still carrying his shield on the left, follows a pace behind her. End with all three on the upper deck, Setzer leading, Celes second, Locke last. Neither Celes nor Locke speaks.
Camera continues smoothly from the incoming composition with only a gentle upward tilt and slight pan right as the actors reach the upper deck, maintaining the same viewing axis and continuous geometry. Keep Locke's stair route visible until he reaches the top; do not hide the ascent behind a new angle or close-up. Reveal only the continuation of the same existing upper deck, not a different vessel or room. Keep the three actors separate in depth, with physical weight, independent reactions and natural cloth movement at normal speed. Audio: exactly the single Portuguese sentence above near the end, soft wind, cloth and individual boot contacts synchronized with steps. No other speech, narration, singing, music, flashes or ship movement.
